patch.value: Read surfaces have no common row contract: field projection reaches 4 of 11 commands and the row collection sits under a different key on each, so no single shell or jq expression works across pm

Measured 2026-07-27 across the eleven read commands an agent or a shell pipeline actually uses: list, next, search, context, deps, graph, get, aggregate, activity, stats, events. Four capabilities decide whether a command can be composed with grep, jq, awk, or xargs. Field projection with --fields exists on four of eleven (list, search, context, get). An encoding choice with --format exists on six (list, next, search, context, deps, get) and is absent from graph, aggregate, activity, stats, and events. Row streaming with --stream exists on two (list, activity). One-row-per-line ndjson exists on four (list, search, context, activity). The newest and structurally richest surface, pm graph with its sixteen subcommands, has none of the four. The second-order problem is worse than the flag matrix. The collection of rows lives under a different key on every command: items on list and search, ready on next, ids on graph traversals, affected on graph impact, groups on aggregate, compact_activity on activity, and a set of scalar buckets on stats. An agent that has learned to pipe one command has learned nothing transferable about the next, and a wrapper script must special-case each surface. The consequence is measurable in tokens as well as in ergonomics: without --fields the only way to get a list of identifiers out of pm graph or pm aggregate is to fetch the full payload and discard almost all of it. This is the projection and row-identity axis specifically. Uniform row streaming as a constant-memory scale primitive is pm-mav1ak, format-flag grammar is pm-srns, the three incompatible list-family json projections are pm-pjnu91, and mode-paired envelopes that report a count beside an empty array are pm-cyrfjq. None of those four asks whether one expression can address a row on every surface.

Every read surface declares its row collection through one contract, so the key that holds rows is derivable rather than memorized per command; --fields is available on every surface that returns rows, and requesting only identifiers costs output proportional to the identifiers rather than to the full payload; A documented one-liner extracts identifiers from any read command without special-casing, and that one-liner is exercised by a test so it cannot silently rot; Surfaces that genuinely cannot project fields state why in their contract rather than omitting the flag; The contract is declared once in the CLI contract layer and consumed by CLI, MCP, and completions, so a new read command inherits it instead of re-deciding it
Make one shell or jq expression work against every pm read surface
Terminal composability is a first-class product requirement; today it is a property of the list family and an accident everywhere else
pm graph shipped sixteen subcommands with none of the four composability affordances, so the gap is growing with each new surface

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fifth projection axis censused 2026-07-29, same shape as the four already recorded here. --summary is accepted by 4 of 18 read commands: graph, deps, health and contracts. It is absent from list, list-open, context, next, get, search, validate, stats, activity, aggregate, events, history, duplicates and test-all. The absence on validate is the sharpest: validate is the most verbose diagnostic in the product and AGENTS.md routes an unsure agent to it, yet the one flag that would bound it exits 2 with Unknown option --summary. So the axis coverage table is now --fields 4 of 11, --format 6 of 11, --stream 2 of 11, ndjson 4 of 11, --summary 4 of 18, and the four commands that accept --summary are not the same four that accept --fields. An agent cannot learn one bounding idiom and apply it; it must memorize a per-command matrix. That is the row contract this item owns, and the --summary column belongs in it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Projection-declaration column measured 2026-07-29, the read-side complement of the --fields column this item already tracks. Five read surfaces declare their projection five different ways. pm list emits a projection object naming mode and the exact field list. pm context emits sections_included and names them honestly - empty at brief, six at standard, ten at deep. pm activity emits only the boolean compact with no field list. pm search emits no projection key at all. pm get emits nothing: at brief depth the envelope outside .item is completely empty and children, claim_state and linked are dropped silently, all three being present at standard. So the same question - what did this shape leave out - has one good answer, one partial answer, one boolean, one absence, and one silent drop. The good answers already exist inside the product, which makes this a generalization job rather than a design job. Note the polarity too: every declaration names what is present, never what is absent, so a caller cannot compute the complement without already knowing the full field set. Omission polarity belongs to the budget contract on pm-5t33or; which key names the projection, and that every read surface has one, belongs here.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Cheap-form census extends this item's row-contract axis with a fourth flag, --summary, measured 2026-07-30. Present and effective on pm health (727 B vs 127,582 B plain, 175x), pm graph impact (488 B vs 223,214 B, 457x) and pm contracts (5,966 B vs 125,193 B). Absent entirely on pm context, which is both the orientation surface the agent guidance routes to first and a 9,067 B default payload with no cheap form at all - pm context --summary exits 2 as an unknown option. So the surface offers a bounded projection on three diagnostic commands and none on the one read that every agent session begins with.

Scope note: this stays inside this item's projection-and-row-identity boundary. It is not the streaming axis, not the encoding axis, not the list-family split, and not the zero-fill envelope class.
